card.name: Break just before a C-a/C-i entry
card.fires_on: Punctuation or a short word that ends one entry and comes right before the next entry starting with C, such as ca-, ci-, or CA. It is seen in style-guide word lists and drug interaction lists.

modes.label: Style guide entries
modes.description: The period ending one entry in an alphabetical usage guide, just before the next C word like calvary or cannon.
modes.example: Callus is a noun for "an area of hard, thick skin<<." >>calvary, cavalry Often confused. Capital

modes.label: Before a C abbreviation
modes.description: An opening parenthesis or similar mark right before an uppercase abbreviation starting with CA or CAB.
modes.example: There are three control signals: RAS\ (row address strobe), CAS\<< (>>column address strobe), and WE\

modes.label: Drug interaction list
modes.description: A word ending a table row, just before the next drug name starting with C.
modes.example: microsomal enzyme activity. 25% decrease Carbamazepine Similar to aminoglutethimide. 30%<< decrease>> Cimetidine Decreases theophyll

card.writes: It lowers C-initial abbreviations like CS, CT and CN, so it seems to steer away from those guesses.
card.plain: It fires at the end of an entry when the next entry is about to begin with the letters Ca or Ci.
